reference_action: Repot baby Frydek into root-ball-sized pot with airy sphagnum/bark/perlite; water thoroughly with substantial drying and reduce watering when not growing. OP later credits advice after a healthy larger new leaf.

sources.reason: Reduce water when leaves are lost and small-container moss/perlite reset overlap reduced watering/smaller airy medium, but drastic cutback is an extra.
Check deep moisture and reduce watering when damp, plus repotting advice, overlap the water-management component; rootbound upsizing is not the target downsizing.
Use draining soil with perlite and ensure drainage for yellowing leaves overlaps substrate correction, but does not give the smaller root-ball pot or near-full drying.
Repot in well-draining mix overlaps substrate component only; routine upsizing and top-inch drying differ from target smaller pot and longer drying.
Remove old soil, rinse roots and repot into draining fresh medium overlaps substrate replacement, although fertilizer-burn rationale and lack of downsizing are incomplete.

actions.action: Add strong grow light if exposure inadequate
Place in small container with moss/perlite

resolved.reason: Reduced water and smaller substrate setup overlap the fix, but the advice is for a damaged white-variegated leafless plant. Unqualified cutback could remove both remaining leaves unnecessarily.

harmfulness.reason: “Cut back” directs an unnecessary destructive step without checking roots or the viable leaves. Tight covering with no ventilation guidance adds risk, although reducing water after leaf loss is sensible.

specificity_accuracy.reason: Small moss/perlite container and “cut back on the water” partially overlap the reference. The main explanations concern white leaves, a dog accident and window light, not this baby plant’s dense mix and root-ball size.

feasibility.reason: Small-container moss/perlite steps are understandable but cutting location and cover management are unspecified. Strong grow lights require an extra purchase.
